source.title: String .toDate() returns the previous day for a date-only ISO string west of UTC

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

`String.toDate()` returns the day **before** the one written when the string is a date-only ISO date (`"2023-06-16"`) and the n8n process runs west of UTC (any `America/*` time zone, for example).

`toDate()` parses with `Date.parse()`, which reads a date-only ISO string as **UTC** midnight, and then forces "00:00h" with `date.setHours(0, 0, 0)`, which works on the **local** fields. In `America/New_York`, `2023-06-16T00:00Z` is `2023-06-15 20:00` local, so `setHours(0, 0, 0)` lands on `2023-06-15 00:00` local. East of UTC (and in UTC) the local day already matches, so the bug only shows up for instances west of UTC.

Other date-only forms such as `"June 16, 2023"` parse as local midnight and are not affected.

The same code is in `packages/workflow/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` and its mirror in `@n8n/expression-runtime`.

### To Reproduce

1. Run n8n with `TZ=America/New_York` (or `GENERIC_TIMEZONE`/system time zone west of UTC).
2. Evaluate `{{ "2023-06-16".toDate().toDateString() }}` in an expression.
3. You get `Thu Jun 15 2023`.

Minimal Node reproduction of the same steps:

```sh
TZ=America/New_York node -e 'const d = new Date(Date.parse("2023-06-16")); d.setHours(0, 0, 0); console.log(d.toString())'
# Thu Jun 15 2023 00:00:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time)
```

### Expected behavior

`Fri Jun 16 2023`: local midnight of the day that was written, in every time zone.

### Debug Info

Found by reading the code on `master`, and reproduced with a unit test that calls `stringExtensions.functions.toDate` directly with `process.env.TZ = 'America/New_York'`.

### Operating System

Ubuntu Linux

### n8n Version

master (current HEAD)

### Node.js Version

20.19.2

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted
